Where the engine says something is wrong with a script without giving up on it. The interpreter's own error() stops the parse where it stands, which is right for a value of the wrong type and far too much for a misspelled class: one typo would take the whole screen with it. So a warning is printed in the same shape as an error, with the same arrows under the place in the file it came from, and the parse carries on. Every note is kept as well, so a test or a tool can read back what a script was told.

```java
import net.tutla.craftytml.client.ctml.CTMLDiagnostics;
```

## Members

### `public record Note(String tag, String message, String where)`

One thing said about a script: what it was about, and where in the file it came from.

### `public static Note warn(String tag, String message, TusanContext ctx)`

Says something is wrong and carries on. ctx is whatever was being interpreted at the time, and only provides the place in the file; without one the note still stands, it just cannot point.

### `public static List<Note> notes()`

Everything said so far, oldest first.

### `public static List<Note> notes(String tag)`

The notes whose tag matches, for whatever only cares about one kind.

### `public static void clear()`

### `public static void printing(boolean on)`

Turns the printing off, for a test that would rather read the notes than watch them go by.
